findings.trigger: Not a displayName comparison bug: both sides of line 24 use displayName(raw keyword), so they agree. The root cause is isStated: isKnown(keyword) is an exact lowercase-canonical lookup, so a display-cased or alias lexicon keyword falls to TextTokens.stem, which only matches single words. The prod backend passes LLM keywords through uncased (apps-backend analyses.ts:132), so 'Power BI' / 'Google Sheets' / 'Stakeholder Management' are never stated in the requirement text or the detail. SKILL 'Power BI or Tableau', keywords ['Power BI'], YES_REGULARLY 'built Power BI dashboards' -> upTo 50 (was 100 at 9be87224, whose stated() lowercased first). Lowercase canonicals ('power bi') work; lowercase multi-word or non-token aliases ('ms excel', 'microsoft power bi', 'powerbi') fail the same way. The stem fallback also skips the lexicon's word-boundary guards: keywordsStatedIn(requirement('C'), 'Wrote C++ code') returns ['C'] (words() yields 'c'), while requirement('c') is empty, so a display-cased short skill (C, R via 'R&D', Go via 'go-to-market') is over-confirmed, a D41 bypass. After #308 merges, its blank-detail AnswerFacts path inherits this and loses the display-cased named skills it confirms today via normalise. Fix once here: `SkillLexicon.normalise(keyword)?.let { it in statedTerms } ?: (TextTokens.stem(keyword) in statedStems)`. Then change the third assertion of powerBiIsConfirmedAsCanonicalAndMatchesAnswerFactsWhenDisplayCased to 100 and drop the stated() lowercasing workaround in KeywordCoverageCalculator. Existing AddUserStatedFactUseCaseTest cases use canonicals and are unaffected.
